utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. The affirmation you made at the beginning of the evidence still applies. And I think Mr. Lukic is to continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, before we continue, may I be allowed to ask a question, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have the impression that when Mr. Borovic was cross-examining me yesterday an error was made. I was wondering if that part of the cross-examination could be gone through and the error perhaps corrected. I could explain what it's about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If you would, please, explain.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At one point in time I was asked about the distance between Sremska Mitrovica and Negoslavci. I'm talking about that portion of the cross-examination. A calculation was made, as to how much time it would take to drive from Mitrovica to Negoslavci and from Negoslavci to Ovcara, and the arrival was set at about 1730 hours. This was linked to a time entry in the notebook saying that the military police were withdrawn at 2230 hours. Both these pieces of information are actually accurate, it's just that the dates don't tally. The first piece of information could have applied in relation to the 19th, but that has no bearing to the actual time recorded in relation to the 20th. I think these two bits of information were actually merged into a single story, and that's not where they belong.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much for that. What I propose, Mr. Borovic, is that at the end of Mr. Lukic's cross-examination, I would allow you, if you wished, to explore that matter further. And if not, perhaps Mr. Moore will. Yes. Is that suitable?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think I may be better placed than Mr. Moore to do that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Lukic. I'm sure both of you, Mr. Borovic, will have a go at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness. We shall now continue. Can I have the usher's assistance, please. I would like to give the witness this set of documents. These are documents that we shall be using. Let us now move to what happened in Vukovar. Based on your notebook, what I saw in your notebook, and also based on what I saw in the operations diary, you arrived on the 9th of November, 1991. It was on the 8th you were given your marching orders, that's what your notebook says.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean in Negoslavci. That's strikes me as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's an exhibit, so we'll be using that. When you arrived at the front line, your company had all its regular tasks, providing security for the commander, for the command post, the check-point in Negoslavci, so what I would like to ask you: Were there any extraordinary or out of the ordinary tasks until the time you were called to Ovcara, or, rather, did the military police company take part in combat operations?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only tell you about the elements who were with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is the element that arrived in Negoslavci, right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Both your answers were yes?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There's something that is a bit unclear in the interpretation. Those elements of the unit who came with you to Negoslavci were the ones going about their regular tasks.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And were not involved in the fighting?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they weren't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Nor was any part of that unit taken away and assigned to another unit for other tasks. They kept going about their regular duties at the brigade command?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I believe you have in front of you Exhibit 371. We could perhaps display it on our screens. This is the operations log of the 80th Brigade. The first page of the operations log, the entry in relation to the 9th of November at 0900 hours. Could that please be shown, Exhibit 371, page 1. You see this, sir, don't you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you please just comment briefly on the entry in relation to the 9th of November, 1991, 0900 hours. CVP, what does it say down there? I suppose that's in reference to your unit, that's as long as you can actually read the handwriting, or do you want me --

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: CVP, this second platoon, is that it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me try to amplify this. "Busy securing the brigade command post. Securing the reception at the command post and protecting the brigade commander."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That tallies with what you said were the tasks of your unit upon its arrival at Negoslavci, right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was the first task that was mandatory.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As we go through this operations log, as I've noticed several different points, when you came there, you submitted daily reports. This is reflected in the entry for the 14th and the 15th of November, 1700 hours. You submitting daily reports. Were these oral or written, the ones you submitted to the brigade commander, I mean?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oral.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, written reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were these submitted on a daily basis?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would usually be late in the day or early in the morning that I would submit a written report, and I did any other reporting in the course of the day, whenever that was necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Commander Vojinovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the commander wasn't there, then I would usually report to the duty operations officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would I be wrong in saying that your military police company came to the front well-rested, they only arrived on the 9th of November, and the other units had been there for over two months, right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I guess you could put it that way. I tend to agree with you on this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It was mostly made up of reserve police officers, I mean military police.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note, could the speakers please kindly try not to speak all at a time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm being asked by the interpreters not to overlap. Please try to keep the same pace that you did yesterday. Do you remember any disciplinary problems in your unit in terms of carrying out assignments?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I guess I could say that everything was all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Reserve military policemen are soldiers who completed their military service and who were trained to be part of military police unit.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not get the last part of Mr. Lukic's answer [sic]. Could Mr. Lukic be asked to speak closer to the microphone. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In addition to this, I suppose all reserve soldiers were sent to military drills, if not to drills then at least they had had some experience on the ground before they were sent to Vukovar to carry out all these new assignments. Would that be a fair assessment?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, now, I might as well agree. You're right, although it would be scandalous for me to talk about everything that was going on. Those were sordid details, but I think we all more or less know what went on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please don't shy away from explaining everything. You are here to tell the truth and we are here to establish the truth. What I want to know is about those reserve officers. Were they trained properly in your opinion and was there discipline in your unit? These are the key questions as far as mobilisation is concerned, in all of that, we all know about that, and that's not something I asked you.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will try to answer your question. This was a newly set-up unit. It was set up early in 1991. It wasn't before I came to Vukovar that I actually saw some of those soldiers. Not everybody responded to each call-up. One thing was certain, everything had completed their regular military term, all of them were trained military police officers for military police platoons. Another thing that I can confirm is there was order, there was discipline, and they were all carrying out any assignments that I gave them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We heard that Lieutenant-Colonel Vojnovic was the brigade commander, and the chief of security was Captain First Class Dragi Vukosavljevic. Do you know what Danilovic was doing in terms of his position and rank?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a lieutenant-colonel by rank, and I think he was Lieutenant-Colonel Vojnovic's deputy.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Chief of Staff?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Chief of Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know who Major Dusan Jovanovic was, does that ring a bell?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My learned friend, Mr. Vasic, asked you about Lieutenant-Colonel Jeftic yesterday, right? You said his office was at the command of the Kragujevac Corps. So you weren't certain if he was actually attached to the corps or to the brigade. Do you know what his position was later on, because you did say that you used to see him later on with General Vasiljevic, but do you know if he had a position apart from his job with the security organ of the corps?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I'm an operative officer, I work with the army. When someone tells me they're an officer, they're an officer, and that's that. I don't wonder about their position or rank.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will assume, however, that your contact with Lieutenant-Colonel Jeftic as rather close. That's why I ask. You don't know, okay. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Another thing, the Kragujevac Corps of the 80th Motorised Brigade, they were part of the 1st Military District; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, probably.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, it's your speed of speaking which is the biggest problem, I think, for the interpreter. Once you seize on a thought you pour it out very quickly. And sometimes it's a long thought. If you could try and slow down. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have been known to be told that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your testimony in chief you stated that the operation -- the 80th Brigade was within the Operations Group South, but I wanted to clarify something. My learned friend, Mr. Vasic, asked you whether you knew that Ovcara at the time was within the area of responsibility of the 80th Motorised Brigade. Your answer was, "I don't know." Mr. Borovic asked you the same question, and your answer then was, "Maybe." You, as the military police company commander, you probably had your own zone within which you carried out your tasks. If someone wanted to send you to the Vukovar Hospital, I presume you wouldn't go. That's why I'm asking this: Did you know that at the time the area of responsibility, including Ovcara, was the area of responsibility of the 80th Kragujevac Motorised Brigade, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was waiting for the transcript. I didn't know that at the time. And yesterday when I said "maybe," the question was put in a different way.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Listening to my question now, did you know that Ovcara was within your brigade's area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please take the transcript from the Belgrade trial, page 73. I believe that is page 72 of the English for my learned friends. You appear as a witness. Towards the end of the page you were examined by attorney-at-law Nenad Petrusic. Was Ovcara, that is the settlement, within the area of responsibility of the 80th Motorised Brigade from Kragujevac. Your answer was yes.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see where that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Page 73, further down. Let's say some 12 lines from the bottom, attorney-at-law Nenad Petrusic. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You appeared in the Belgrade court as a witness?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You testified under oath, and you know what the implications of that are?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You are also testifying under oath here?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please clarify these two different answers you provided to the same question.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At even then, as now, I am somewhat confused. What do you mean by the area of responsibility? Do you have in mind the place where we worked and where we moved about? If that was the gist of the question, yesterday and today, then that includes the field where we worked. When I said "no," that I understood to be who was the most senior officer for that area, whether that was the operations group or the motorised brigade. If I call something an area of responsibility, that means that the military police company was tasked to cover the entire area of the 80th Motorised Brigade. That's why I said yes and my answer today is yes. But if you had in mind who was the most senior officer in the area, I don't know. Maybe that clarifies why I responded with a yes and a no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I just interrupt for one moment. I know it's very difficult for defendants to remain still. But I know that Mr. Mrksic has been vigorously nodding his head either to agree or deny when answers are given. I would be awfully grateful if that could just be -- if he could just not do that. I am sympathetic to the position of defendants, but sometimes it gives a wrong impression to a witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Mrksic, I see your acknowledgment. Thank you, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was interrupted by Mr. Moore. I don't know whether his reaction was necessary, given the circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I didn't ask you about the commander for the entire sector.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, it was. Okay? Now, I would like today to avoid the tension that developed yesterday, particularly between you, Mr. Lukic, and Mr. Moore. So if we could just keep things a little calm. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have resolved our tensions at a later stage yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The Ovcara sector, was that within the zone of your brigade's units?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's how I understood the question then. And now I understood it completely differently. Both yesterday and today.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you arrived at Negoslavci you reported to Vojnovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your statement given to the OTP I have read something, and a question wasn't asked of you concerning that. While you were at Negoslavci you stated that you were assisted by the local TO units, I presume at these points that were established. My question is whether you had any sort of problems regarding those units.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was a TO unit in Negoslavci. At day-time they carried out their routine duties in various houses, and during the night they assisted in additional guarding duties that needed to be established for night-time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you had no problems cooperating with them?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You have described to the OTP the command post of your brigade. Did I understand correctly that you said that Mr. Sljivancanin used to come there -- or, rather, that you said that he was somewhere close to where your command post was?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both. He used to come by to see the commander, and that he was in the vicinity, at the other end of the street. I believe that's where he used to spend the night.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: During those days when you were at Ovcara, in and in front of the hangar, you didn't see Sljivancanin?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At the time in or around the hangar on the 18th, 19th and the 20th, did you hear from anyone that Sljivancanin was coming by?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What sort of uniforms do the military policemen wear when carrying out their duties? And I have in mind the relevant time in Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In early 1991, up until the end, all the units, including the military police, wore olive-drab uniforms. But the military policemen could be distinguished by their white belts.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And, therefore, your military policemen had white belts?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us now go back to the Belgrade trial on page 73 regarding this topic that is of interest to me. For my learned friends from the OTP, I wanted to read out a portion from page 72. Mr. Vezmarovic, have you found it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what to look for.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Four lines from the top. I will believe with the previous page to give the context. You were asked by Natasa Kandic: "Were the Mitnica prisoners secured by members of the military police of the 80th Motorised Brigade or were there also policemen of the guards brigade there?"

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: "That is members of some other units as well?" Your reply: "If I understood the question properly, you asked me ..." Then the judge: "The first day, the first group." Your reply: "Were the first and the second group secured by only the 80th Motorised Brigade? Yes." Natasa Kandic, attorney-at-law, appearing on behalf of the defendants: "Did your soldiers wear white belts?" The judge: "The question was asked." Natasa Kandic: "What about those from the guards brigade, the policemen, did they wear?" Your reply: "Answer, yes." Natasa Kandic: "So there was no difference in the uniforms?" No. Your reply was: "No, no, you should bear something in mind." Then the judge's question: "Are there any differences in uniforms?" Your reply: "Perhaps if I can reply, that was the uniform." And then the presiding judge says: "Yes, go on with your reply. Were there any differences in terms of uniform between the members of your unit and the members of the police of the guards brigade?" I provided some comment to explain the context. And then your reply: "That's what I tried to -- uniforms were the same for the entire Yugoslavia at the time, if I may say so. That means in Slovenia, in Croatia, in Macedonia, in Bosnia, in Montenegro, in Serbia, we all wore the same uniform. Meaning all from the military police had the exact same uniforms." And the remainder of your answer is not important for this line of questioning. This confirms what I asked you about your unit before, and I wanted to ask you whether you abide by what you stated in the Belgrade court; that is, that all of your military policemen and all of military policemen in general wore white belts.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, all policemen had white belts. But at wartime they could also wear the usual belts. The standard issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: To move on to another topic now. Who was your immediate superior in terms of command?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Commander Vojnovic and the organ of security, that being Lieutenant-Colonel Jeftic and Dragi Vukosavljevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In terms of the security organ, in what sense were they your superior, or rather according to what rules?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the military police my only contact was with the security organs in terms of drills and the wartime tasks. That contact was a superior who would issue tasks and assignments, controlled my work, and apart from that person, the commander would do the same as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what the basic rule is for all the soldiers and officers of the JNA? What sort of regulations were in force, what text-book?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your question. What is the name of the document, you mean? Well, what do I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you want me to remind you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The rules of service.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It regulates all types of relationships and structure within the JNA.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps I may call it a rule book of sorts, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What were the basic rules of the military police at the time? Were those the rules of service for the military police of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we please have a document, 65 ter document, I believe it will be tendered by the OTP. It is 397. The rules of service of the military police from 1985. Could we have page 9 on the screen for the witness, the ERN number being 0207-2100.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I believe that's within the set of documents I provided.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will look for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You have it in front of you on the screen as well. I will read slowly Article number 12. "The military police is commanded and controlled" -- just a minute. "Control and command over a military police unit is exercised by the officer of the unit or institution within whose establishment the military police unit happens to be, or to which it has been attached." We shall move on from there, but first let me ask you about this article. In your specific case, your military police unit, who was in command of your military police unit, under Article 12, what's your interpretation?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think Vojnovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I agree with you completely. Let us now go to Article 13: "In the technical sense a military police unit is under the control of the security officer of the military unit or institution within whose establishment the unit happens to be, or to which it has been attached. He makes proposals to the military unit officer or to the institution for the use of military police forces and is responsible for the combat readiness of the military police unit and the execution of tasks. While exercising control over a military police unit, the security organ officer from paragraph 1 of this item has the same rights and duties as the officers in the branches and services of the military unit or institution in terms of control of the various units of the branches and services." Under this provision of Article 13, who was the officer formally in control?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have said before, Jeftic and Dragi Vukosavljevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Lieutenant-Colonel Jeftic, given that he was physically in the brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If he was, in fact, attached to the corps, then it would have been Dragi Vukosavljevic, right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Based on what I have just read out to you, especially Article 13, is it indicated anywhere that the security organ is in command of the military police, even as far as technical aspects of its work were concerned?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is not indicated anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So they are in charge of the technical aspects of your work, they make proposals to the commander about special regulations without going into any detail on that, but they are not in command in terms of the military police, they do not command the military police?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says. Is that what you wanted to hear? Because that is what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would the chief of security have been able to issue any orders without the commander's approval?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How can I be expected to know that?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you receive any order from the security organ without checking with your commander?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: While we're at it, the next page, paragraph 14. Paragraph 14 talks about the SSNO unit in charge of security, which is in charge of the technical aspects of the work of the military police. Among other things, it inspects the training of military policemen, makes proposals and takes measures to promote its work, is involved in organising formations of the military unit, and is involved in any assessments concerning the combat readiness and work of the military police. What you said yesterday in relation to Jeftic, does this bear any relation to Jeftic's peacetime activities with your unit? If you remember. If not, not.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I quite understand your question. I'm not sure what sort of an answer you're expecting. In peacetime conditions, I was only in touch with the security organ, and that was the only body whose assignments and orders I was carrying out. Which I continued to do in wartime.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document as a whole into evidence, because we will all probably be using it, the Defence as well as the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit 435.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No problem. It's something that you had no say in, Witness. I see that you have the document with you, right? The rules of service governing the work of the military police?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, these are my notes from a lecture, Lieutenant-Colonel Relja Ristic [phoen]. Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Vojnovic was your commander?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You obeyed his orders, you executed his orders. Based on what I heard, it worked like this: Based on your testimony so far, when you arrived in Negoslavci you reported to Lieutenant-Colonel Vojnovic, right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On the 18th he told you to go and look for a facility that would be appropriate for temporarily holding those prisoners, right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: He agreed with the proposal, it didn't matter whose proposal it was, but eventually he agreed that the hangar should be used for holding those people, right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: He was the one who ordered you to clear the hangar and to get it ready for the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: He was the one who told you to wait there and meet the prisoners there. That's what you said before the court in Belgrade, right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could we please have Exhibit 371 placed on our screens for a second. This is the operations log of the 80th Brigade. The page number is 0D00-0615. Could we please zoom in on the 18th of November, 1600 hours. Further down. I'll read this out loud. The handwriting is a bit tacky, but this is what it says: "Group 1 with four trucks with about 70 Ustashas arrived in the detention unit. During the night another hundred were brought in." That's not what I'm interested in. "Lieutenant-Colonel Rade Danilovic was appointed commander of the camp. Most of the brigade's officers took part in the -- in setting up the security regime." Did you know that at 1600 hours on that day Chief of Staff Lieutenant-Colonel Rade Danilovic was appointed camp commander? Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you see him there when the prisoners came?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. He probably was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Nobody told you that he was the camp commander?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You say that when Vojnovic introduced you to Karanfilov he said, this is something you stated some days ago on the 8th of May. He said Karanfilov was in charge of transporting those persons, that they would be spending the night there. And that your superior officer would be Karanfilov in terms of that particular security job. You stated this two days ago. You remember that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: First of all, you said yesterday when you mentioned those persons coming and asking questions, based on what you said two days ago, I see that you said they would be spending night there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Mitnica group.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And the next day they would be leaving, right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I was told. That they would be spending the night there and that probably the next day, at about 8.00 Karanfilov would be there and then ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This assignment that Vojnovic gave you, when he told you about the fact that you would be receiving orders for that particular operation from Karanfilov, this was over the next day when you handed those persons over to Karanfilov, when he took charge, right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And as you said yesterday, you informed Vojnovic accordingly when you were given the typewritten list when you came to him, when he told you that that list should be taken to Mitrovica, because those people had gone already?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This new assignment was given to you by Vojnovic, right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let's go back to the 18th. What I was asking you about was the next day. Mr. Vezmarovic, you're saying before this Court that your task was in terms of the orders for securing those persons, that this assignment was issued to you by Vojnovic at Ovcara when they arrived outside the hangar; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Are you sure Vojnovic was the one who told you that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure about the words that were actually spoken, but what happened was we talked, we were introduced, and he said that Karanfilov would now be taking charge of the whole thing. I don't remember the exact words spoken at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You don't remember the words, you don't remember the nitty-gritty, but you are sure that the person was Vojnovic, right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This decision that your commander made, for the orders for that operation, for providing security during that night to be taken from an officer who was not from your unit, so this decision by your commander, was this something that you entered into your notebook?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I made a note to the effect that I would be contacting Karanfilov, Captain Karanfilov and where, the place where he would be.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We have seen that. But did you note down the fact that the officer in charge and the officer giving you orders was not someone from your unit? Is this fact something you wrote down at the time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you record this in your daily report, if, in fact, you produced one on that particular day?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the first 10 days or perhaps the first five or six days it was done on a regular basis, the daily reports, and then it stopped. I don't remember, actually, producing a written report at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What about the fact that you were taking your orders from an officer who belonged to a different unit, did you tell the duty operations officer at the brigade?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you ask him later on whether he had been informed by anyone else?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You say you didn't know that Danilovic was the camp commander, but you did know that he was Chief of Staff. Did you perhaps tell him about this?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let's go back to your statement, the statement that you gave to the Novi Sad investigating magistrate during the Ovcara investigation for the Belgrade tribunal. This was on the 24th of June, 2004. The pages numbered and our page is page 2. This is passage 4, on that page in English. Have you found that, sir, the Novi Sad statement?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is the fourth -- what is passage number 4?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The one that's been highlighted, "The same afternoon." It's with investigating magistrate Alimpic, and the date is the 24th of June, 2004.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Page 2, the passage reads: "The same afternoon."

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's actually the first.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, "the same afternoon"?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Slowly. "The same afternoon, on the same day Lieutenant-Colonel Vojnovic told me that the first group of prisoners would be arriving. I took along between 15 and 20 men from the company under my command, and I came to Ovcara. Military buses were soon there carrying prisoners. This was when I was told that I would be taking my orders from Captain Karanfilov, a security officer. I did not know which exact unit he belonged to. I know that one of my superiors told me about it, but I do not know exactly who it was." This was a year and a half ago, wasn't it? Is this something you remembered later on, that this was Vojnovic, or did you know at the time but simply didn't wish to clearly say, or perhaps the person was not Vojnovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you talking about a different paragraph? New paragraph, new thoughts, new questions, new issues arising. I don't think this new paragraph is in relation to previous one.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So what does the word informed about that, what does this word "that" mean?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know what the question was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please, could you go through that paragraph again and tell me if it's out of context or not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've gone through it and there must have been a question preceding this answer, I think. That's a logical assumption. It's not like I was doing all the talking. They were asking questions and then I was answering the judges and also everybody else.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Hold that thought. I wish to clarify what exactly the procedure was.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Even if we look at it this way, it changes nothing about what I said. If I remember well. I know that -- what exactly does it say? I know that one of the officers told or bold or sold me about it, but I don't know who exactly. I don't know what can really be challenged about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'll ask you a simple question then, if you don't think anything can be challenged. Did you or did you not state under oath in Novi Sad that you did not know who had told you to report to Karanfilov and that you would be taking your orders from Karanfilov?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't remember. I think both words have the same meaning, at least as far as I'm concerned. But well, there you go. In any other statements I made, any later statements, I am saying the same thing. I don't know who told me that. This is the only time I said I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vezmarovic, you provided a lot of statements. I suppose you were doing your best to tell the truth every time, right?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I suppose you know, and I suppose you were cautioned by Judge Alimpic about the potential consequences of perjury?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So you were telling the truth, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So as the document seems to suggest, and you signed this document, did you tell Judge Alimpic that you didn't know who had told you about Karanfilov, whereas right now here you are saying that it was Vojnovic, right? That's all I'm asking you about, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what I'm trying to say. At this point in time what is indicated here does not clash with what I'm saying. I clearly indicated here that Vojnovic was not the one who told me that. Is my interpretation correct as far as you're concerned?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can I phrase my question differently. When you gave your statement in 2003, did you know that Lieutenant-Colonel Vojnovic was your commander already?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You were not prepared to mention his name, or is it the fact that he simply didn't tell you at the time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did tell me, but I didn't say here that he didn't tell me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let's not dwell on this anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Could I just draw the Court's attention to -- and Mr. Lukic, to -- it's page 24, line 24. I don't know if this is a correct translation, because it was travelling quite quickly. This is what I'm trying to say at this point in time what is indicated here does not clash with what I'm saying. I clearly indicated here that Vojnovic was not the one who told me that. Perhaps I'm missing the point. I thought the witness was saying that Vojnovic had actually told him that. I don't know if it's a mistranslation, but it clearly is something that may become important, or I may be missing the point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Moore.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: If one looks at 25/9, actually, there is an inconsistency there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The position is not clear on the transcript. And we had avoided interrupting your cross-examination, but may we point out two things: First, the Chamber hasn't a copy of this transcript. So on issues like this we are not in a position to assess the force of what you're saying. Hence, it's been our practice for copies to be made available to us, even if in the end they're not tendered as an exhibit. It enables the Chamber to follow the evidence and see where the strength and the weaknesses are. The second matter to remind you that there was established a practice that if there were to be military regulations dealt with, we would be provided with a hard copy. So the military police regulations we haven't got. I was waiting until the end of the session to mention those things to you, but as you have been interrupted, I thought I'd get them off my chest now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, I misunderstood your instruction to receive a hard copy of the documents. I believe it only pertained to such military experts as Mr. Trifunovic was. Also, so far we haven't given you any statements because you yourself stated that you didn't want to refer back to the statements, although I would prefer you to have them before you. And I will do my utmost to provide copies for you after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vezmarovic, based on what I read out to you and what you stated before the investigative judge, saying that you don't know which one of the officers told you to report to Karanfilov, you signed this statement, you stated that. Is that indeed what you stated to the investigative judge in Novi Sad, simply yes or no?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you want me to remember what I said, I can't. But it doesn't say clearly here that I wasn't told by Vojnovic. This is a new paragraph, meaning a new topic. Why would there be a new paragraph? I didn't say that Vojnovic didn't tell me that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I have to read out yet again, the Judges no longer have that portion of the transcript before them, so I will read out slowly. "On the same day, the same afternoon Lieutenant-Colonel Vojnovic told me that the first group of prisoners was to arrive. I took along some 15 to 20 members of the company I commanded to Ovcara. Soon the military buses with prisoners arrived. And I was told then that I was to receive an order from Captain Karanfilov, who was a security person, although I don't know which unit he belonged to."

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: End of paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: A new paragraph. "I know that one of the officers told me that, although I don't know who exactly."

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you are going to go through the entire paragraph, this is another conversation between Karanfilov, myself and officers. Croatian officers, as the witness put it. Therefore, that was another topic I discussed. This is no longer the first conversation. I can't recall exactly, but going through the text now, and if you are to look at the text, this is no longer the first event, but the second one. Because the first one didn't include any Croatian officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I want to ask you yet again. Did you state this in front of the investigative judge and signed the statement. You said one of the officers told me that, but I don't know who it was exactly?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it states here. But I also tried to explain as to the question whether I don't know if I was told that by Vojnovic, we can't make that inference on the basis of this sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In that context, in front of the investigative judge in Novi Sad, did you mention Vojnovic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. I haven't seen any of these papers since 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Before the arrival of the convoy on the 18th, the Mitnica group one, you provided security and you assigned them to different posts; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Did you say before their arrival?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We were only planning. Theory is one thing and practice is another, and indeed it was different.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you determine where the guard positions were supposed to be and where the people were to be put inside the hangar?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Karanfilov gave you no order as regards the type of security or an increase or decrease of security as well as the number of people needed to organise it?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll try to be as brief as possible in my answers, but I have to say the following: You are asking me about details that I really can't recall. It has happened so many years ago. We are now talking about whether at quarter past 4.00 my left or my right hand was in one of my pockets. I'm going to tell you that no, he didn't give me any instructions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you to state here what you can remember, but on the other hand you clearly indicated what instructions he gave you, and I can see that you remember some details, so perhaps you can provide answers to those. Let us move on. This is what you stated two days ago as having been told by Karanfilov, that is the transcript pertaining to the 8th of May on page 79. You stated the following: That Karanfilov told you that these were captured Croatian soldiers who had surrendered at Mitnica that day. That they had all been disarmed. That one of them was allowed to keep his pocket-knife. That you were to abide by the Geneva Conventions. That among the members of the group there were some officers who were accorded a separate status according to the Geneva Conventions, and that they were to be picked up the next morning by someone. And, as you stated, he provided his first and last name and point of contact for the night. That's what you stated two days ago?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is there anything else he told you when you met for the first time, and something you may have forgotten to say, and perhaps you can remember some more now?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be brief, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You will agree with me, Mr. Vezmarovic, that everything I listed here were instructions and information belonging to the routine tasks of a security person informing an officer; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You probably meant when he was supposed to issue an assignment to me. Then yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you receive an order from him?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand. What sort of order?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Everything I listed. And apart from that, did Karanfilov issue an order to you at that point?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, of course. He ordered me to treat the prisoners according to the Geneva Conventions, that was an order.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That was an order?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Simply put. Could I explain, perhaps? I am here as a witness, and I may be told I have the right to clarify, I was told to stand up when the judges enter. He didn't order that -- for me to do that, but he said those were the rules.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As an officer and a military policeman, you know what the rules of service of the military police have to say regarding the security of prisoners, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm just waiting for the transcript. All you're trying to ask me is in the field of theory. I'm trying to explain the practice. And you keep on asking me about theory.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Are you trying to say that you don't know what the practice was as regards the Geneva Conventions and that you didn't know that until you were told by Karanfilov? Is that what you're trying to say?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I sense some tension here. I'm trying to say that I did my work as best I could as an officer. And what I had been taught, not much of that could have been implemented or put in practice. I did my best in carrying out my duties though. As the result of that, until the 15th of December not one of my soldiers was killed or injured. We completed all of our assignments, things were fine. That's what I was trying to say. And as for theory, well, I also accept that I may have made mistakes as an officer. Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I believe you have already provided an answer to this, and if you did, I apologise. But I wanted to ask you whether all the brigade officers were there, including Dragi Vukosavljevic on the 18th at 4.00 p.m., or around that time?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My interpretation is the following: I did my job as best I could. There were many officers of different rank. I can't be specific as to whether he was or wasn't there. If someone puts it to me that he was, I accept that, provided I am uncertain about seeing him someplace else at the same time. So if you mention Dragi Vukosavljevic, I accept that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You can state yes, no, or I don't remember, but you can't really say I accept your proposition. If you don't remember, you don't remember.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe the question was put in such a way that granted me that type of an answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Am I mistaken if I say that in keeping with the regulation that you are probably familiar with, that the security organ can only provide professional advice on the completion of a task to the military police unless the commander has transferred some of his powers to the security organ to be able to issue commands?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are referring to rules of service, and yet the last portion of your question is not something that can be found within the rules of service. To reiterate, we have theory put on paper. If we are to deal with theory, then we can interpret regulations. I believe things are put in the right way for as long as they are not changed. And I tried to implement that. But let us not discuss practice.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us not discuss practice then. If you were ordered something by an officer from another unit, would you receive such an order if you were not told by your commander to do so?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I understood you properly, you asked me whether I would accept an order by an officer from another unit without my commander notifying me of that.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear the end of the witness's answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The answer was "no."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As you testified here and in Belgrade, you stated you didn't know what unit Karanfilov was from?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You said that Vojnovic told you so ...

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It is my position here that Karanfilov issued no orders to you and that he couldn't have, but that he could only provide professional advice, as the security organ. And that is also what was confirmed by Karanfilov in his various appearances before various tribunals. Would you say that I was wrong?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: I object to the way that question is put. It is my learned friend putting in evidence. If he wants it to be done, he should call Karanfilov.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Moore is entirely correct, Mr. Lukic. And I think you are aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. I apologise. I wanted to mention this: This witness was put all of these facts before. That's why I mentioned what he said in previous trials when asked about these things.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Am I mistaken if I were to say that Karanfilov could not order you, but rather that he could only issue instructions or advice? Am I mistaken?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your immediate superior, Mr. Vojnovic, in your opinion, did he have any reason to try to cover up those facts or to confuse people as regards Karanfilov and the orders? Did he ever say anything like that to you?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Lieutenant-Colonel Vojnovic is an officer with whom I had occasional contact. And your question implies chats, having chats with the lieutenant-colonel, which I didn't have.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Without chatting away with the lieutenant-colonel, without having coffee with him, did you still discuss this topic? Did you talk to him about what he has to say about that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Out of all the conversations, outside courtrooms and various institutions and buildings, starting with the restaurant in Kragujevac and ending with this situation here, I believe I talked to him only once or twice regarding this. And after such a conversation he cleared some things for me concerning a part of day that I was uncertain of. And Novica clarified it for me. I accepted what he had to say, and I believe it to be the truth, and that is that we went to Nemci.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you were returning from your testimony in Belgrade, he said that you were taking money to Nemci and that's how you remembered, and this is Novica Trifunovic I'm talking about?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't go in the same car, but we spoke during the break there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: To conclude with this topic before the break, when you've completed your tasks on the 19th and the prisoners were handed over to Karanfilov, and when you were told to type out the list you compiled, did he or anyone else tell you at the command that there was another group of prisoners coming? I believe you've already provided your answer to that.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: According to your knowledge, your traffic police platoon, was it, did they participate in the transport of any group? I have in mind the Mitnica group from or to Ovcara, or the Vukovar Hospital. Did your traffic policemen ever participate in such transfers?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: None of the military policemen participated in securing the convoy.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we have a break now, and then I will start with another topic right after.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We will resume at 20 past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Vezmarovic, yesterday, or actually the day before, you testified in response to a question by Mr. Moore about the events in the course of the night, the first night when some people came and they wanted to know who the people inside were, and then you said that according to you it was normal for them to come and to express an interest in the prisoners, and according to you this was just a normal conversation with these people. My question is: The next day, when you reported to Karanfilov during the takeover, did you convey this fact to him in the same way, did you tell him at all, and did you do it in that way, about the arrival of those people in the course of the night, when those people came to the hangar and about whether there were any problems there or not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would like to repeat what I already said. And that is that in the report to Captain Karanfilov it said that the security was proper, there was no violence, there were no major problems. I don't know whether I told him all the details. I don't recall that. But the point of the report was that the security during the night was carried out according to the regulations, and it was done properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's how I understood it, but as far as I remember, you don't recall specifically whether you told him about the arrival of those people or not, but if you do remember perhaps, did you point that out as a problem to Karanfilov or not? If you don't remember, it's okay, we can continue.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we for a moment look at your notebook, page 63. We looked at that yesterday. You talked about the entry with the list. After the list the entry stating received on the 18th of November, 1991, around 1600 hours, and so on and so forth, it's clear and, I don't think that this was in dispute, that this was written by someone else, and this was something that Judge Parker asked you about, whether this was your handwriting or not. I don't think it was your handwriting?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if I didn't say it at the time, I'm telling you now, that is my handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In that case, I apologise. It didn't seem to me as if it was. But tell me, you said that you wrote this down yourself, the names of the prisoners by their name, first, last name and their numbers; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And what comes after that is your handwriting too; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And if I am not mistaken, I don't know if I said that here. I said that I used both alphabets competently, and that I wrote the first and last names of prisoners initially in the Cyrillic, but then when I realised that it was complicated because of the names, then I switched to the Latin script.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did I read that somewhere, I can't remember where, somewhere in your statements that you said that the first six officers were noted down, and then you gave that to somebody else who was writing down the names, and then the number didn't tally because that person didn't put their own name down. So when you got to Sremska Mitrovica it didn't work out. I mean, it's not such an important detail, but perhaps if that was so, maybe you will remember and tell us.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the story relates to one of the soldiers who -- well, it's interesting only as a kind of a joke. The story was that the number of the prisoners was -- the same number was not handed over as was the number on the list, but it was more of a joke. They were just joking at my expense. Because at the time that they were talking, I requested all the prisoners to be taken out again, and then I called out their first and last names and the story ended because then we drank coffee at the end. But the list was --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: And the interpreter didn't catch the last part of the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. We won't go into that anymore. We don't need this document on the --

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, the interpreter said that she did not catch -- hear the last part of the answer. Perhaps that could be clarified.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The witness said that he made the list, and that that was his handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you say that, sir?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I made the list myself that evening, and that complete part is in my handwriting. These pages that you have.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... just to complete the question, the list that you prepared, was it correct or was there a deficiency in the list?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The list was correct. They were just joking with me at one point in time. It was 181 or 185 soldiers, and six officers. That's what it was on the list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Did you mean 185? I think earlier you said 175.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 175 soldiers, plus six officers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you handed them over at Mitrovica and then when you came back, I assume that you informed the officer on duty at your command that the assignment had been carried out?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I don't remember who it was that I informed; maybe it was Lieutenant-Colonel Vojnovic, maybe it was the officer on duty. In any event, I did stop by at the command.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you recall telling Karanfilov about this? Do you remember being in touch with him or in contact with him after you came back from Mitrovica?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw Captain Karanfilov on the 11th in the morning and on the 20th in the evening at Ovcara. Other than that, I didn't see him anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So the answer is no?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Again, I'm sorry to rise. I got on the 11th in the morning. I can't help but think there is an error either in translation or what has been said.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that the witness actually made a slip. He said -- he meant to say the 19th but didn't say that.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what it says, but I can say it again. I saw Karanfilov on the 19th in the morning and on the 20th in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm just going put one more question to you, not in relation to your testimony, but in relation to somebody else's testimony that we heard here. That night, of the 18th and the 19th, did you see there, in front of the hangar, in that area or closer to the yellow house, or anywhere where you were able to see, did you see any vehicles arriving with civilians, with men and women who were there for some time and then left in buses? Do you recall seeing anything like that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Again, with the utmost respect, my recollection is that there wasn't evidence for the night of the 18th/19th. I thought it dealt with the 19th. But anyway, the answer deals with the timetable. That certainly is my recollection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That, I think, is part of the point of the witness's concern which he expressed at the commencement of this evidence today. Whether there was confusion between the 18th and the 19th in the evenings. So we will leave it to Mr. Lukic for the moment and then Mr. Borovic, and then if there is anything left, it will be Mr. Moore to sort out.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I asked this specifically about the night of the 18th and the 19th when the Mitnica group was being guarded. And I would like to remind Mr. Moore that this was in relation to a witness who testified before the Tribunal a while ago, that that evening a group came from Mitnica on the 18th, and there were some other people there too and then they left. I'm just saying what this protected witness said. But let us continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could we now place on the monitor Exhibit 371 again, page 0D00-0616. We are going to, once again, look at the operations diary of your brigade entry for the 19th of November at 1200 hours. I am going to read it here, the entry for 1200 hours, the 19th of November. "We have been informed that a decision has been made that the prisoners and members of the ZNG should be handed over to -- should be transferred to Sremska Mitrovica." That's right. "Lieutenant-Colonel Danilovic has been relieved of duty to guard members of the MUP and ZNG in the Ovcara sector." Is that what it says there?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You have already responded that you don't know if Lieutenant-Colonel Danilovic was commander of the camp. Does this entry perhaps refresh your recollection about a decision being made at 12.00 noon to disband the camp?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't have the recollection, but may I say something? What you have read means, as far as I understand, that he's being relieved of the duty of escorting the convoy. I assume that before that it says that he was assigned the task of escorting the convoy. Perhaps that's an entry an hour or two before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, it doesn't say that. All it says is that he has been assigned as commander of the camp, but we will see about that later. But let us assume that he was, according to the diary, the commander of the camp. Now we are going to move to the 20th of November when you went to Ovcara once again. Based on your testimony, I concluded, Mr. Vezmarovic, that when you came to your unit first that's where you heard that a number of your military policemen were already at Ovcara and that they were guarding a new group of prisoners, and you, on your own initiative, which is how I understood it, you went there to see what was going on. Did I understand your testimony correctly?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know why you say on my own initiative.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did anybody order you to do that?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am in command of the unit, the unit has a task that it is carrying out, so I went there to see what the unit was doing. There's nothing strange about that. Perhaps if you want to go back to the theory of command, maybe we can then refer to continuity of command.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. You mentioned your soldiers Predrag Sapic and Novica Trifunovic a little bit earlier. You said that Trifunovic was a person who had actually refreshed your recollection. The soldiers who were with you and went -- are those the two soldiers who left Negoslavci in the Pinzgauer with you to go Ovcara?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't want it to seem as if I am saying one thing at one time and something else at another time. This conversation with Novica, well, as far as that's concerned, I don't remember who left with me, but Novica explained to me that he left with me, that he and Sapic went with me, that when we went to Nemci and then when we got to Negoslavci, then we -- they continued Ovcara.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, just tell us what you remember. If you don't remember something, you can say that.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So what that means is that I cannot really tell what true memory is and what is an augmentation of something that I really experienced. So in myself I cannot tell these things apart. I know somebody came with me, and he tells me, and judging by some incidents that happened on our way to Nemci, I know that he was with me. So if he was with me in Nemci, we came to Negoslavci after that, and after that it follows that he was with me. But what I'm saying, it's because of these earlier statements that --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember or did he remind you that he was in front of the hangar during the security at the time when you were there, both him and Sapic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, again, we have this thing that we know what happened, but I'm not sure exactly who it was. There were soldiers there, there was security there, standing outside, and he told me that he was outside. I don't know exactly whether that was so or not, but that's what he said, that he was outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember whether he told you -- first of all, I'm going to ask you: Do you remember that you sent him and Sapic later from Negoslavci in the course of the night to secure the military facility at Ovcara? Do you remember that? Do you remember ordering that, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I think that no order was issued to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that Trifunovic told you that he went to Ovcara during the night, Trifunovic and Sapic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If you didn't issue that order, who could have issued that order, since they were soldiers in your company?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander, but again I'm telling you it was the security organ.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Specifically, Vukosavljevic?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Probably the duty officer conveyed the order to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You will agree with me, earlier you said you went to Ovcara to be with your soldiers, so I must conclude that you always need to know where your soldiers are. If someone else sent them there, would that person have had to inform you that some of your soldiers had left in the course of the night in accordance with an order by the commander to carry out some assignments? Do you remember that or not?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I understood this question properly, it's something along the lines of what would happen if it were to happened [as interpreted]. I don't know that the order was issued, and I don't know that they were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, we're not going to make any assumptions here. Now we're going to look at the same page of the operations diary, or possibly the next page, it's page 0D00-0616. Six. You also talked about this with Mr. Vasic yesterday. We're talking about the 20th of November now at 1600 hours. I'm going to read slowly what it says there. "The commander of the brigade" -- this is 1600 hours on the 20th of November. "The commander of the brigade requests that guard shifts or that officers are relieved in order to guard the captured ZNG members and the MUP members. The company of the military police was engaged on this as well as officers of the brigade command." Now, what I would like to ask you is this: According to this entry from the diary, who is asking that shifts, guard shifts be relieved?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're asking me to interpret something that isn't mine. Am I supposed to be an expert here?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think it's a simple question.

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not saying it isn't simple, but I'm not familiar with the document, and yet you're asking me to interpret this. This entry was made by whoever happened to be duty officer at the time. As soon as they had time, they would write it down. They did have a number of other things to worry about too. The time-line is not necessarily accurate either. It always says 8.00, 9.00, but it may as well have been quarter past 8.00 or six minutes past 3.00 in the afternoon or whatever. I suppose this was written pursuant to an order by the commander ordering them to do something else on top of this, and the action taken is described here in this entry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm not asking you to act as an expert. It seems that a military police company was involved in the execution of this order, so who could possibly have ordered this to the military police company?

utterances.speaker: DRAGAN VEZMAROVIC [Resumed]
